title: One-Pot Tomato Spinach Pasta
description: Short pasta simmered right in a garlicky crushed-tomato sauce, then finished with wilted spinach, basil and grated cheese. No draining.
scaleNote: A 5 to 6 quart pot fits this batch. When doubling, use a bigger pot so the pasta stays under the liquid, and allow a few extra minutes for it to come to a boil.
equipment: Large, wide pot or Dutch oven with a lid

image.alt: Illustration of a pot of short pasta in tomato sauce with spinach

ingredients.prep: finely grated, plus more for serving
ingredients.note: a Parmesan-style cheese made without animal rennet

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large, wide pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and a pinch of the salt and cook, stirring now and then, until soft and translucent, {time 6-8 min}.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook, stirring, until the garlic is fragrant and just starting to turn golden, about {time 1 min}.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, broth and water, then add the pepper and the rest of the salt. Raise the heat to high and bring to a boil.

Stir in the pasta, pressing it under the liquid. Once it returns to a boil, lower the heat to a steady simmer, set the lid ajar and cook, stirring every couple of minutes so nothing sticks, until the pasta is tender and the sauce has thickened, {time 14-18 min}.
If the pot looks dry before the pasta is tender, stir in a splash of water and keep simmering. If the pasta is done but the sauce is still thin, simmer uncovered for {time 1-2 min} more.
Turn off the heat. Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until it wilts, then stir in the cheese and the cream, if using.
Let the pasta stand for {time 2 min} so the sauce thickens slightly, then stir in the basil. Taste, add more salt if needed and serve with extra cheese on top.

notes: Pick a pasta shape with a package cooking time of {time 10-12 min notimer}. Very thin shapes turn mushy, and large ones like rigatoni need more liquid and time.
Tomato sauce catches on the bottom of the pot easily, so keep the heat at a steady simmer rather than a hard boil and stir often.
Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 3 days. The pasta keeps absorbing sauce, so add a splash of water when reheating.
